reason: It makes the small cat the subject of declarative “add,” merging the opening placement fragment with the subsequent directive.
It links “says” to the girl’s desire to switch. The complement of “says” is “it suits her.”
It captures the grid lines and plot edge but marks bare “have” and participial “clipped” as declarative clauses within the causative construction.
It treats the first “fit” as a condition on the next step. “If you could fit” introduces the embedded question after “I wonder.”
The circuit makes connect an imperative within the thought complement, while should governs both make and connect. It also leaves the clause about the boxes reading as one step unattached.
It gives “you” as the maker, attaches the Website redesign label to the orange rectangle, and captures the separate acknowledgment.
The imperative routes that arrow around Verify now, with instead plausibly marking Verify as the alternative landmark.
It preserves the modal question and records the full “car Goal” noun phrase as the object of “add.”
It places three cats along the bench but attaches “facing right” to the bench instead of the cats.
It preserves the modal question with “you” as subject, “add” as predicate, and “a bird” as direct object.
The two imperatives place the new bench by the tent and the lantern on the bench. “That” can refer to the bench in the first instruction.
The graph captures the woman and the one-spot move to the right, but attaches the yellow hat to the move instead of using it to identify the woman.
It records the sun as subject and “what” as the question word, but leaves the questioned endpoint of “on” unexpressed as a role.
The circuit marks the command to make the chart as nonfinite and makes the rank column the object of “share.” Ties share the rank, and the rank column is to be shown.
The imperative takes the striped pattern as its object and places that pattern over the small rug.
The imperative takes an ear as its object and preserves all three modifiers: large, big, and pale.
The circuit correctly identifies the background statement, the Harbour group, and the half-transparent result, but marks the command “set” as declarative.
The modal question asks you to create an orange hexagon, links the Membrane label to the hexagon, and captures the thanks.
The imperative takes the poster as its object and specifies “shorter” as the result.
The circuit makes “90th” modify cost and “percentile” modify claim, splitting the statistic “90th percentile.” It also leaves “starting at zero” unattached to the y axis.
The circuit makes “labelled” a declarative complement of “make.” The yellow diamond is the object to make, and “labelled Q1 plan” modifies that diamond.

The circuit preserves the modal question and two bars per region, but attaches the year comparison to the bars as a nominal adjunct. The comparison specifies which periods of regional revenue to show.
The circuit marks the bare infinitive “be” after “let” as declarative and attaches “facing right” to the hand-width measurement instead of the girl.
The imperative makes all boxes the subject of the embedded predicate “glow.”
The effect is the direct object of “strip,” and the “off” relation identifies the sign as the removal source.
The purpose relation incorrectly includes “keep everything else.” That imperative coordinates with “change the avatar,” while only looking happier is the purpose of the change.
The embedded “if” clause preserves “you could rest,” one red block, and its destination in the gap under the shelf.
The circuit preserves the apology and the “but” link to the imperative, with the markers as the object and small circles as the endpoint.
The imperative gives “Put” the peak as its object and “a calllout” as its destination.
The modal question identifies “Team update” as the item to replace and links it to the full quoted replacement through “with.”
The “on” relation locates the turning event on the house. In the source, “on the house” identifies which bird should become a big brown owl.
The circuit treats “what I need” as an embedded question. It is a free relative identifying the needed item as one flow chart about the customer refund process.
The graph captures the booking and the team's reason, but attaches “tomorrow morning” to “like” and “short” to “planning.” Both qualify the meeting being booked.
The farm's “with” relation reaches only the shed. The graph uses apposition for the other entities where the source coordinates all four as things the farm has.
The draw imperative specifies a big, ringed planet and places the drawing to the left of the indicated lake.
The slice labels are the subject of “want,” the “on” relation links them to Budget split, and the complement specifies a medium distance.
The graph gives both step counts, but “back” scopes over the shared “take” predicate, whose object includes both step groups. The source limits “back” to the first two steps.
The graph preserves the “can you” question and identifies the caps, but makes “bigger” a modifier of the error bars. The caps are what should become bigger.
The give imperative identifies “me” as the recipient and a greenhouse next to the house as the object.
The reverse imperative takes “the last thing” as its object and preserves “last” as the qualifier.
The graph identifies the dots on the dashed line, but attaches “wider” to the relation with the revenue trend. “Wider” describes the desired state of the dots.
The direct object is Sales, and the by relation leads to chart. The chart should be the direct object, with Sales by region identifying it.
The scene participants are mislinked through apposition. The boy is attached as an appositive of the cabin, and the deer and the girl–cat group are attached as appositives of the boy.
The between relation is anchored to a nominal headed by smack. The farmer is the participant standing between the horse and the tree, and smack modifies that placement.
The graph captures both groups of three, but attaches around to the entities and the when clause to the last group. These expressions modify the turning.
The imperative places a curling stone under the tree and accounts for please as courtesy.
The imperative makes a space shuttle, with a placement relation to the right of the mountain.
The modal question asks whether we can cut the sales chart to the top six and gives the reason that the deck template has no room for a table.
